raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38516.

SGLang's fused diffusion JIT kernels need an NVIDIA GPU of the Ampere generation or newer (SM80+: RTX 30-series / A100 and up). On older cards — Turing and before, like the issue reporter's RTX 2080 Ti — image generation still works through the Triton/torch fallback paths, but the code never checked the GPU generation up front: each kernel launched a full nvcc compile that could not succeed, waited for it to fail, and only then fell back. On the reporter's FLUX run that cost ~49 seconds on the first denoise step, and the failed-compile output (pages of `rsqrt` header-conflict errors) made it look like something was broken when the fallback had actually worked fine.

This PR adds the up-front check, so unsupported GPUs skip straight to the fallback with a one-line log message. The `rsqrt` header conflict itself is an NVIDIA-headers-vs-glibc bug; the sglang-side mitigation is tracked separately in #45066.

## Modifications

- New `kernels/ops/diffusion/common/jit_arch.py` with `require_sm80()`: checks the detected GPU generation and raises before any compiler work when it is below SM80. AMD (HIP) and Moore Threads (MUSA) pass through, since their capability numbers are not on NVIDIA's SM scale.
- Called as the first step of the 16 diffusion JIT kernel builders that had no generation check (14 under `kernels/ops/diffusion/`, 2 under `kernels/kda_kernels/`), copying the pattern already used in `vdn_delta_factors_jit`. The raise is caught by each kernel's existing build-failure fallback, so behavior on unsupported GPUs is unchanged — the fallback just engages instantly instead of after a doomed compile. Kernels already gated at SM90/SM100 are untouched.
- Docs: a Troubleshooting entry in `docs/docs/references/faq.mdx` covering the glibc 2.42 `rsqrt` compile failure (workarounds, link to the distro patch) and the SM80 floor (the issue's third suggested fix).
- Regression test `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_jit_sm80_floor.py` (CPU suite, no GPU needed): simulates an older GPU via `override_jit_cuda_arch(7, 5)` and asserts the compiler is never invoked, and pins the cutoff at exactly 8.0. Both cases fail on the pre-fix code and pass with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel arithmetic changes. Verified on an L40 (sm_89):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place.py
# 13 passed in 207.92s (cold cache; ~24 JIT modules compiled through the new gate)
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_jit_sm80_floor.py
# 2 passed
```

With the GPU generation overridden to sm75 on real CUDA tensors, `residual_gate_add2` falls back immediately with `diffusion CUDA JIT kernels need SM80 or later; detected sm_75`, and the fallback output matches the plain PyTorch path bit for bit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On pre-SM80 GPUs, the fallback now engages in milliseconds instead of after serial failed nvcc builds (~49 s on the issue reporter's setup; not re-measured here — no Turing hardware available, and the fix removes the compile attempts entirely rather than speeding them up). On SM80+ the check is one cached capability read per kernel builder, evaluated once per process — effectively free.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

       you can try to decrease `--mem-fraction-static`, decrease `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`, or decrease `--chunked-prefill-size`.
 - Other bugs, please file an issue on GitHub.
 
+### JIT kernels fail to compile with rsqrt errors
+
+On distributions with glibc 2.42 or newer (Ubuntu 25.10, Fedora 43, Arch), every JIT kernel build can fail with nvcc errors like:
+
+```text
+/usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/bits/mathcalls.h: error: exception specification is
+incompatible with that of previous function "rsqrt"
+(declared at .../include/crt/math_functions.h)
+```
+
+glibc 2.42 added host `rsqrt`/`rsqrtf` declarations that conflict with the ones in the CUDA headers (still present in CUDA 13.1). This affects every GPU generation. SGLang falls back to Triton/PyTorch implementations after each failed build, so generation still works, but the first request pays for the failed compile attempts.
+
+Until NVIDIA ships fixed headers, you can:
+
+- Run SGLang in a container whose base image has glibc older than 2.42.
+- Patch `crt/math_functions.h` in your CUDA installation to add `noexcept (true)` to the `rsqrt` and `rsqrtf` declarations, as several distributions do ([Gentoo's patch](https://gitweb.gentoo.org/repo/gentoo.git/tree/dev-util/nvidia-cuda-toolkit/files/nvidia-cuda-toolkit-glibc-2.42.patch)).
+
+Also note that the fused diffusion JIT kernels require compute capability 8.0 (Ampere) or newer; on older GPUs SGLang skips the JIT build and uses the fallback implementations directly.

+"""SM80 capability floor shared by the diffusion CUDA JIT builders."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import get_jit_cuda_arch
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.common import is_hip_runtime, is_musa_runtime
+
+_MIN_SM_MAJOR = 8
+
+
+def require_sm80() -> None:
+    """Refuse pre-SM80 CUDA targets before any nvcc build is attempted.
+
+    No diffusion JIT kernel supports pre-SM80 GPUs, so a build attempt there
+    only burns tens of seconds of nvcc time per module before failing (measured
+    ~49 s on the first FLUX denoise step on sm75). Raising here reaches the
+    same per-op build-failure fallbacks instantly. HIP/MUSA capability numbers
+    are not SM versions and pass through.
+    """
+    if is_hip_runtime() or is_musa_runtime():
+        return
+    arch = get_jit_cuda_arch()
+    if arch.major < _MIN_SM_MAJOR:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "diffusion CUDA JIT kernels need SM80 or later; "
+            f"detected sm_{arch.major}{arch.minor}"
+        )

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import override_jit_cuda_arch
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.common.jit_arch import require_sm80
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.rope import qknorm_rope_jit
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=6, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def test_pre_sm80_skips_jit_without_compiling(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """On pre-SM80 GPUs every diffusion JIT build fails, but only after tens of
+    seconds of doomed nvcc attempts on the first denoise step (#38516). The
+    capability gate must reject before the compiler is ever invoked."""
+    compile_calls: list = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        qknorm_rope_jit, "load_jit", lambda *a, **k: compile_calls.append(a)
+    )
+    with override_jit_cuda_arch(7, 5):
+        ok = qknorm_rope_jit._can_use_fused_qknorm_rope(
+            head_dim=256,
+            rope_dim=192,
+            is_neox=False,
+            dtype=torch.float16,
+            cache_dtype=torch.float16,
+            round_norm_before_rope=True,
+            pack_kv=False,
+            cache_has_full_width=False,
+        )
+    assert not ok
+    assert not compile_calls
+
+
+def test_sm80_floor_boundary() -> None:
+    """The floor is exactly SM80: Ampere passes, the last pre-Ampere arch raises."""
+    with override_jit_cuda_arch(8, 0):
+        require_sm80()
+    with override_jit_cuda_arch(7, 5):
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="SM80"):
+            require_sm80()
